title: Analytic: vertical dipole above a PEC ground plane, image interference (3D FDTD)
description:
A z-oriented electric point dipole (current moment Il = 1e-12 A m, gaussian pulse at 1 um) at height h above a perfectly conducting ground (em_fdtd_3d, 25 nm cells): bc_z_lo pec plus a pec_domain on the next cell layer, so the conductor fills z < 2 dx and its surface (the pinned tangential E) lies at z = 1.5 dx; CPML on the four side faces and on z_hi, the ground running into the side layers. The dipole sits on the E_z face at z = n_up dx, h = (n_up - 1.5) dx; the study sweeps n_up over 6, 10, 14, 20, 26 (h = 112.5-612.5 nm). A flux box from z = dx (bottom face inside the conductor, zero flux) to 0.95 um collects the power radiated into the upper half-space.
Analytic (image theory: dipole plus its in-phase image 2h below, half of the pair's power goes up): P / P0 = 1 + 3 (sin(u) / u^3 - cos(u) / u^2), u = 2 k h = 4 pi h / lambda, P0 = eta0 k^2 (Il)^2 / (12 pi) of the free dipole; P / P0 -> 2 as h -> 0 (1.814, 1.446, 1.103, 0.914, 0.999 at 1 um for the five heights). The image is exact on the Yee lattice (mirror plane on the tangential E nodes).
Sweep tab: P_ratio (1 um) and P_ratio_long (1.2 um) vs n_up with the dashed references.
Spectra tab: em.radiated_power quantity power_per_cw vs the dashed P0(lambda) P / P0 over 0.8-1.3 um.
Expected agreement: ~0.2-0.5 % (lattice dispersion and box quadrature as dipole_far_field, CPML reflection of the grazing wave along the ground); to be confirmed by a first run. No far-field pattern: near_to_far assumes vacuum outside the box.
